title: Java List Sorting
learningObjectives: Sort a list with Collections.sort or List.sort.
Use natural ordering for comparable values.
Provide a Comparator for custom ordering.
Sort strings without confusing case or locale rules.
Keep sorting predictable and test equal-key cases.

understand.concept: Java lists can be sorted in place. Collections.sort(list) and list.sort(comparator) arrange elements according to natural ordering or a supplied Comparator. Natural ordering for numbers is ascending and for strings is lexicographic. Comparator.comparing can sort objects by a selected property, and reversed can invert an ordering. Sorting changes the list itself; make a copy first if the original order must be preserved.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic helps Java developers select and use the right standard-library tools for java list sorting in maintainable applications.
understand.analogy: Think of the collection or date API as a purpose-built tool: its operations communicate the guarantees your program can rely on.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a guide; Java API contracts, equality rules and exception behaviour determine the actual result.

explain.narrative: For values with a natural order, call Collections.sort or List.sort(null). For custom rules, pass a Comparator such as Comparator.reverseOrder or Comparator.comparing. Use thenComparing to define tie-breakers. A comparator should be consistent and avoid subtraction-based integer comparisons that can overflow. Sorting is in place, so any other variable referring to the same list observes the changed order.

questions.explanation: The list passed to sort is reordered.

questions.prompt: Which interface represents a custom ordering rule?
questions.explanation: Comparator defines an external comparison strategy.
It reverses the natural comparison order.
It applies another comparator when the first comparison is equal.

questions.prompt: How can you preserve the original list order?
questions.answer: Sort a copy of the list
options: Sort a copy of the list
questions.explanation: Sorting a separate copy leaves the original unchanged.
